doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

chapter: Cello group, family and the road
title: Ventura's Open House club on the White Horse Pike
summary: Ventura calls them to rejoin at his club near Philadelphia, and they move to New Jersey.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Then at one point Charlie Ventura called us again and said, “listen, I have a club in New Jersey, I would like to have the original group, put it back together, would you guys care to join us?” Now we had an apartment in Chicago, and I had been playing solo piano at a little joint, just to make a living, while our first child was growing. And so we said hey this is a good way, because I’d been doing that for about a year and a half, different places around Chicago, playing for acts, doing this, writing, playing for singers, and —
It sounded like a perfect opportunity.
We said great, yes, we’ll do that.

Because we could also move there. He had his own club, it was called Charlie’s — what was it called? Open House. And it was on the White Horse Pike outside of Philadelphia, and so it was sort of a semi-permanent thing. We worked there every weekend and he would bring in a comedian from New York City and put on a show and it was a big sort of a white elephant club out on the highway. It was a great place. It had a great stage and a great dance floor, so it was a fun place people came out to. He did very well there for a while. I think he had it for a few years. So we went back there and worked with him. And we got an apartment there, and we subleased something, didn’t we? Or just leased something I should say. I think we had a two or three year lease in an apartment there. So we stayed there for a while with him and that was good.
